title_en: Inside the Revival of Venture Capital Liquidity with an Industry Pioneer
title_zh: Hans Wildens（Industry Ventures）谈风投流动性复兴
subtitle_zh: 风投二级先驱 Hans Wildens 解析流动性困局与 Goldman Sachs 合并决策
summary_zh: 本期 Goldman Sachs Exchanges 的 Great Investors 系列由 Michael Brandmeyer 对话 Hans Wildens——他围绕风投流动性难题创建 Industry Ventures，将其做成约 70 亿美元在管资产的风投二级（venture secondary）龙头，并于 2026 年 1 月与 Goldman Sachs Asset Management 合并。Wildens 拆解流动性危机：公司留在私下的时间越来越长、退出放缓，LP 只问'何时能拿到钱'。他指出现有风投组合里两股力量交叉——AI 驱动的增长与被 AI 冲击的非增长，加上净值（NAV）估值高低分化被放大；资金向前 25 家明星公司集中，而 3 万家私营公司中靠后的流动性极差。McKinsey 等估计存量基金沉淀逾万亿乃至三万亿美元，即便 IPO 恢复到每年约 50 单也不够，于是延续基金（continuation vehicle）、配合回购要约（tender）的结构化安排大量增加交易量。他观察到卖方从早期的困境卖方（distressed seller）转向获利了结与组合再平衡，基金周期拉长到约 14 年、分配金额腰斩。展望上他判断二级规模终将超过一级（其他资产类别皆如此），数字 AI 与实体 AI 融合是诱人机会，并坦言做基金管理比做软件公司难，因为退出周期长、须跨回撤反复证明自己。是一堂风投二级市场机制与流动性的深度课。
description: Inside the Revival of Venture Capital Liquidity with an Industry Pioneer

turns.en: One thing that's interesting in our market that's starting to happen is that even participants in the secondary market are starting to get liquidity through secondaries, which historically had never happened.
turns.zh: 我们市场里有一件很有意思的事正在发生——即便是二级市场的参与者，也开始通过二手份额交易获得流动性，这在历史上是从未有过的。

turns.en: There's so much capital sitting in the system that it's not enough liquidity to give back to the market. And so we think that the venture growth market on the secondary side of the market can be larger than the primary.
turns.zh: 系统里沉淀了太多资金，光靠正常的退出机制根本还不够把流动性还给市场。所以我们认为，风投成长期（venture growth）在二级端的规模最终可以超过一级。

turns.en: I think this is one of the most exciting times I've ever seen for investing, and I think we're just beginning in it. Welcome to Goldman Sachs exchanges.
turns.zh: 我觉得这是我所见过的投资领域里最激动人心的时刻之一，而我们才刚刚开始。欢迎来到 Goldman Sachs Exchanges。

turns.en: Great investors. I'm Michael Brammeyer. Venture capital has a liquidity problem. Companies are staying private longer, exits have slowed, and limited partners are asking a simple question, when do I actually get paid?
turns.zh: 《Great Investors》。我是 Michael Brandmeyer。风投行业正面临一个流动性难题：公司留在私下的时间越来越长，退出速度放缓，有限合伙人只问了一个很简单的问题——我到底什么时候能拿到钱？

turns.en: My guest Hans Wildens built industry ventures around that question, growing it into a leading venture secondary specialist with roughly $7 billion in assets under supervision, before agreeing to combine with Goldman Sachs asset management in January of 2026.
turns.zh: 我的嘉宾 Hans Wildens 正是围绕这个问题创建了 Industry Ventures，将其发展成一家拥有约70亿美元在管资产的行业领先的风投二级（venture secondary）专业机构，随后在2026年1月与 Goldman Sachs Asset Management 达成合并。

turns.en: Today, how severe is the venture liquidity crunch? What's real in AI, and why he finally said yes to being acquired? Hans, welcome to great investors.
turns.zh: 今天我们聊：风投流动性危机到底多严峻？AI 里什么是真实的？他又为什么最终答应了被收购？Hans，欢迎来到 Great Investors。

turns.en: Thank you for having me. For our listeners that may not be focused on secondaries all the time, if I'm an early entrepreneur, if I'm an early VC investor, or even a later stage investor, what are the reasons that people are selling to secondary players like you?
turns.zh: 谢谢邀请。对于可能不是经常关注二手份额的听众来说——如果我是一个早期创业者、一个早期风投投资人，甚至一个后期投资人，人们把股份卖给像你们这样的二手买家的理由有哪些？

turns.en: The reasons have been changing over time. When we first started 26 years ago, most of it was to stress sellers, sellers that no longer wanted the investments anymore, like a corporate venture capital fund decided to terminate their investments and then sell the portfolio, or a hedge fund decided to stop making private investments and just concentrate on liquid securities and sell their private portfolio.
turns.zh: 理由是一直在变的。我们26年前刚起步的时候，大部分是困境卖方（distressed seller），就是不想再持有这些投资了——比如一个企业风投基金决定终止投资然后清掉整个组合，或者一个对冲基金决定不做私募投资了，专注做有价证券，就把私募组合甩出来卖。

turns.en: A lot of it was distressed sellers, just exiting things they didn't need or want anymore. Then that evolved over time to include sellers that had made a big gain.
turns.zh: 很多都是困境卖方，就是想退出那些他们不再需要或者不想要的东西。后来逐渐演变了，包含了那些赚了一大笔的卖方。

turns.en: I would say a vast majority of what we've been purchasing over the last 10 years has been giving gains to investors. We also have been buying portfolios at losses to the original cost as well.
turns.zh: 我觉得过去10年我们买的大部分交易都是卖方在获利出场的。当然我们也确实在亏本——相对于原始成本——买过一些组合。

turns.en: I would say that that's tilted over the last 10 years so that you see sellers using the market for portfolio rebalancing or profit taking or risk management if a single position in their portfolio outweighs everything else that they can trim it.
turns.zh: 我觉得过去10年天平在倾斜，你会看到卖方利用这个市场做组合再平衡、获利了结、或者风险管理——比如他们组合里某一个头寸比重过大，他们就可以减一减。

turns.en: More traditional portfolio management reasons to sell securities. Let's go down one level to what's actually happening in existing venture capital portfolios because if you talk to investors, be they entrepreneurs or limited partners or venture capitalists, there's just a huge illiquidity problem out there.
turns.zh: 更传统的组合管理卖出理由。我们再往下一层看看现有风投组合里到底在发生什么——如果你去跟投资人聊，不管是创业者、有限合伙人还是风投家，大家说来说去就是一个巨大的流动性问题。

turns.en: What's going on? Is it a problem of Marx? Is it a plumbing? What are the big issues that you're seeing that are holding us back from a liquidity standpoint?
turns.zh: 到底怎么回事？是并购（M&A）的问题？还是管道（plumbing）的问题？从流动性角度看，你看到哪些大问题在阻碍我们？

turns.en: I think it's everything. There's a cross-current of AI growth and non-growth due to AI in the private market. That's one issue. I think the NAV marks, some of them are undervalued, some of them are overvalued, and that's becoming more extreme of whether or not something's very overvalued or very undervalued because of the way NAVs held in the funds.
turns.zh: 我觉得是所有问题都有。私募市场里有两股力量在交叉作用——AI 驱动的增长和被 AI 冲击的非增长，这是一个。然后还有净值（NAV）估值，有些标的被低估、有些被高估，而且由于基金里 NAV 的估值方式，这种高估或低估正在变得更加极端。

turns.en: I think there's also concentration in the market now around certain names. You're seeing a lot of crowding in the top 25 private names. In the market, when you go beyond the top 25 private names and there's 30,000 private companies, the market gets pretty illiquid.
turns.zh: 我觉得现在市场还存在向某些标的集中的问题。前25个私募明星公司聚集了大量资金，但如果你往前25名之后看——市场上有3万家私营公司——后面的流动性就非常差了。

turns.en: Then in terms of M&A and IPO activity, which has been challenged over the last five years, we're starting to see that accelerate, but there's so many illiquid companies and so much NAV as illiquid, I think McKinsey came out and said they thought it was over a trillion in prior funds and then other people came out and said, it's over three trillion in prior funds.
turns.zh: 然后在并购和 IPO 活跃度方面，过去五年一直不太景气，我们开始看到在加速。但是太多公司处于低流动状态、太多 NAV 是缺乏流动性的——我记得 McKinsey 出来说他们认为存量基金里有一万多亿美元，然后其他人又出来说三万多亿。

turns.en: There's so much capital sitting in the system that even a few IPOs or let's say it normalizes to 50 or so IPOs per year, it's not enough liquidity to give back all the capital into the market.
turns.zh: 系统里沉淀的资金太多了，就算有几单 IPO——假设恢复到每年50单左右的正常水平——也不够把资金还给市场。

turns.en: You're seeing a lot of structuring around secondaries in the primary financing events with tenders in the companies, seeing a lot of restructuring of funds with CVs, you're seeing a lot of LPs exiting different funds at different times to get cash to fund other funds they're funding and so that that's just generating more trading activity.
turns.zh: 你会看到大量围绕二手份额做结构化安排——比如在一级融资事件中配合公司回购要约（tender），还有通过延续基金（continuation vehicle）做基金重组，很多 LP 在不同时间退出不同基金套现然后用这些钱去投其他他们正在出资的基金——这些都只是在增加交易量。

turns.en: Given all this illiquidity, what are you seeing with buyer and seller expectations and does it depend on when the companies were funded? It's really interesting.
turns.zh: 在这种流动性紧张的环境下，你看到的买卖双方预期是什么样的？跟公司的融资时间有关系吗？这个真的很有意思。

turns.en: I mean, there's a cohort of older companies that haven't seen acceleration, they've seen de-acceleration with the AI technologies being adopted because budgets shifting away from what they were doing or maybe a lot of the AI coding technology can kind of replace what they were, what they built and then you're seeing the exact opposite in some older companies where they've rebuilt their tech stack to be AI first and resold that into their current
turns.zh: 就是说，有一批比较老的公司没有加速，反而在减速——因为 AI 技术被采用之后，预算在从它们做的事情上转移走，或者很多 AI 编程技术可能直接替代了它们原来建的东西。然后你也看到完全相反的另一个情况——一些老公司把技术栈重构成了 AI 优先（AI first），重新向现有的

turns.en: customer base and seeing dramatic acceleration and adoption of their new AI technologies within their customer base and so you're seeing hyper growth.
turns.zh: 客户群推销这些 AI 产品，在客户群里看到了爆发式的增长和采用，所以你看到了超高速的增长。

turns.en: I'd say it's very interesting from an investment perspective because some older businesses that haven't been able to energize themselves and re-architect their tech systems are falling behind when others are actually taking advantage of this new wave and cross-selling and upselling all the new AI technologies and developing to their customer base and so that's happening.
turns.zh: 我觉得从投资角度非常有趣，因为一些没能自我革新、重新架构技术体系的老企业正在掉队，而另一些企业真正在利用这一波浪潮，交叉销售和向上销售所有新的 AI 技术产品给现有客户群——这一切正在发生。

turns.en: It's hard for investors to see that and then in terms of the bar taking a company public today you have to be so large so growth has to be a certain rate, a lot of the people participating in the IPO market want to see profitability and growth metrics combined.
turns.zh: 投资人很难看到这些差异。然后从上市门槛来看，今天你要做到非常大，增长率要达到某个水平，很多参与 IPO 市场的人想看的是盈利和增长的组合指标。

turns.en: That's just caused more pressure in terms of the companies to stay private longer. You've also had the businesses themselves and the founders decide to stay private longer in the secondary market and the way that liquidity can be had now is enabling them to do so and so in a weird way our secondary market has enabled some of these companies to stay private longer because if they want to get liquidity to their employees or to their shareholders
turns.zh: 这给公司造成了更大压力，让它们留在私下的时间更长。另外，公司本身和创始人也主动选择更长时间保持私有——现在二级市场能提供流动性，使得他们能够这样做。所以从某种意义上说，我们的二级市场反而让一些公司能待得更久，因为如果它们想给员工或股东提供流动性，

turns.en: they can do through the secondary market therefore there's not a need to go to the public markets. So let's orient our listeners to what does a venture secondary really mean? People talk about directs, people talk about buying portfolios, but orient us to the types of opportunities that you see in the secondary market today. Yeah, I think that that's a great question.
turns.zh: 它们完全可以通过二级市场实现，所以就不需要去公开市场了。那我们来帮听众理一理——风投二级到底意味着什么？人们常说 directs（直接转让）、买组合，但给我们梳理一下现在二级市场上有哪些类型的机会。嗯，我觉得这个问题很好。

turns.en: There's so many different secondary transaction types today that you can kind of bucket them into three buckets. The first bucket are direct secondary transactions so these are single stock positions in companies or multiple stock positions in multiple companies but they're the actual stock certificates and ownership interests in the companies that are being traded so that's the direct secondary market much like the NASDAQ right you can buy with single stock or you can buy
turns.zh: 今天二级交易的种类太多了，大概可以分成三个大类。第一类是直接二手交易（direct secondary）——单一公司的股份头寸或者多个公司的多个头寸，交易的是实际的股票凭证和所有权权益，这就是直接二手市场，很像 NASDAQ 嘛，你可以买单个股票，也可以一次买

turns.en: multiple stocks at once and then there's the LP part of the market which is buying limited partnership interests in the venture funds and so the venture funds hold the same stocks that are being sold on the direct secondary market but they're held in a fund in a commingled structure.
turns.zh: 多个股票一起买。第二类是 LP 层面——买风投基金的有限合伙份额。这些基金持有的股票跟直接二手市场上卖的其实是同一些，只是放在了基金里、以混合结构持有。

turns.en: Sometimes there's one company left, sometimes there's 50 companies left in the fund interest but the fund interest is basically your transaction with a limited partner that's in a fund and then you're buying that their ownership interest in the fund that in turn owns the company and then the third part of the market is what I like to call special situations which are things like continuation funds that's a fund at the end of its life or midlife that is doing a continuation
turns.zh: 有的基金只剩一家公司，有的还有50家，但基金权益本质上就是你跟某个 LP 之间的交易——你买他在基金里的所有权，然后这个基金又拥有那些公司。第三类市场我喜欢叫'特殊场景'（special situations），比如延续基金——就是基金到了存续期末或中期，在做一个延续

turns.en: vehicle or a portfolio continuation from the vehicle itself and basically resetting the time period and you can even reset the portfolio construction of what's being purchased in a CV or continuation fund. One of the things I find remarkable about the venture industry today is as it becomes more successful in an interesting way it actually becomes less liquid and today the average company that's venture backed that goes public takes 14 years I mean that's an eternity
turns.zh: 载体（continuation vehicle），把基金本身的投资组合延续下来，基本上重新设定时限，在 CV 里你还可以重新构建要买的组合。我觉得风投行业现在有个特别值得注意的事：它越成功，流动性反而越差——今天一个风投支持的公司平均要14年才能上市，那简直是永恒。

turns.en: and so you think about the venture market without the secondary market it's almost hard to imagine right now. Yeah I think that this has become very structural where if a limited partner or a direct shareholder or a fund manager wants to get some sort of liquidity before a normal exit of an IPO or M&A event they're looking for liquidity on the secondary market. The adoption of this from not only the smaller funds that are holding these securities at large gains but also
turns.zh: 所以你想想看，如果没有二级市场，风投市场几乎无法想象了。是的，我觉得这已经变得非常结构性了——不管是 LP、直接股东还是基金管理人，只要在 IPO 或并购这种常规退出之前想要流动性，他们就会去二级市场找。这种趋势不只是那些持有大幅浮盈的中小基金在用，

turns.en: from the larger funds that have been in them for a long time and deployed lots of capital into them we think is going to continue in different formats and what's largely being driven by the whole period being 14 years long. I think there's also an issue with the last five years and we've seen the amount of distributions coming out of the venture funds get over halfed so traditionally we have 20% or so per year of distributions and we've gotten down to five to 10% a year on average over
turns.zh: 那些持有时间很长、投入了很多资金的大基金也在用，而且以不同形式持续下去，这很大程度上是因为整个基金周期变成了14年。我觉得过去5年还有个问题：风投基金分配出去的金额减少了一半多，传统上每年分配20%左右，但过去5年降到了平均每年5%到10%。

turns.en: the last five years so you have even more of a constraint in terms of the capital just compounding on itself and being a liquid. Let's talk about your approach to pricing risk within the secondary market. I mean this is one of the things I find really fascinating because I'm a lifelong investor and secondary investor but I'm typically pricing cash flows. Let's start with the AI part of venture portfolios which is growing very very quickly right now. There's a lot of businesses
turns.zh: 过去5年降到了平均每年5%到10%——所以资金一直在自我复利，流动性更加受限。我们来聊聊你们在二级市场里怎么给风险定价吧。这是我特别感兴趣的一件事——我作为一辈子做投资的人，也做过二级投资，但我通常是对现金流定价。我们先从风投组合里 AI 相关的部分开始，现在这部分增长特别特别快。有大量公司

turns.en: that are getting funded. There is a lot of fundamental growth. There's also a lot of growth that feels like it might be a little bit secular so talk a little bit about how you go about pricing some of these very exciting companies which have gotten very big very quickly. How are you going about pricing these assets? I'd say the pricing exercise has been very similar to what we've been doing for two decades in terms of venture itself compared to other asset classes has a
turns.zh: 正在获得融资。确实有很多基本面的增长，但也有很多增长你觉得可能更多是受结构性大趋势推动。聊聊你们怎么给这些发展迅猛的明星公司定价？这些资产是怎么估价的？我觉得定价方法跟我们做了20年的一直很类似。风投本身相比其他资产类别，定性判断在承保（underwriting）里占比更高——

turns.en: higher component of underwriting in qualitative assessment and so you're dealing with how large you think a market is going to be, how durable you think the product is going to be, what their competitive moat is and how can that be extended or defended over time. It's something that has existed in technology since it started so that's not new. I would say the thing that might be new in this phase is that we haven't seen the rapid adoption, the rapid growth and the rapid cash
turns.zh: 你要评估这个市场未来有多大、产品持久性如何、竞争护城河（moat）是什么、以及这个护城河能不能延展或防御。这在科技行业从诞生起就一直存在，不新鲜。我觉得这个阶段可能比较新的是——我们以前没见过这种快速采用、快速增长、快速产生现金流

turns.en: flow generation and then while they're in the private market they get disrupted. The technology shifts and changes are if something else is invented by a competitor that they might stall out and then start going negative growth while they're still private. It happened episodically before but it wasn't something that would happen to the whole market. You're buying private securities, they're growing, you're seeing multiple expansion, you're seeing extreme valuation expansion but then
turns.zh: 然后在还在私募市场里的时候就被颠覆了。技术变化迭代，如果竞争对手发明了什么新东西，它们可能在没上市的时候增长就停滞了，甚至开始负增长。以前也有零星的案例，但不至于影响整个市场。你买的是私募证券，它们在增长，倍数在扩张，估值在极度扩张——但同时

turns.en: while they're still private, you're seeing potentially contraction due to competitive threats and things. That's new because the pace of all these new technologies is compressed the time period of success and so it'd be interesting to see if a lot of these businesses don't go public, if they're going to have durable growth and moats over time or if they're going to get disrupted. Is that related to the analysis here? We talked about 30,000 companies
turns.zh: 还在私下的时候就可能在收缩——因为竞争威胁之类的原因。这是新现象，因为这些新技术的节奏把成功的窗口期压缩了。所以很有意思的是，很多公司不上市的话，到底能不能维持持久的增长和护城河，还是会被颠覆。这跟你们分析的方法有关吗？我们之前说到了3万家

turns.en: being funded over the last decade, decade and a half. Maybe a thousand or 2,000 of them are AI funded in the last few years. That still leaves 25,000 plus that were funded effectively pre-AI. I guess extend that thinking into how you're analyzing the companies that were founded before AI was front of mind for everybody including venture investors. I think there's a great investment opportunity and a small cohort of those companies where they still have amazing
turns.zh: 公司——过去十到十五年融资的。可能其中一两千家是最近这几年跟 AI 相关的融资。那还剩25000多家基本上是在 AI 成为所有人——包括风投——的关注焦点之前创立的。能不能把这种思路延伸到你们怎么分析 AI 时代之前成立的公司？我觉得在一小部分这样的公司里存在很好的投资机会——它们仍然有出色的

turns.en: founders, great management teams, good technical talent where they've been able to pivot if they're in a vertical, if it's a vertically-oriented SaaS business or if it's a vertically-oriented services technology company and then incorporating and building out all the new AI technologies in that vertical. They have a chance of becoming extremely fast-growing, extremely profitable, more efficient with their people in terms of just their cost structure can be less.
turns.zh: 创始人、优秀的管理团队、好的技术人才，他们能够转型——如果是垂直领域的，比如某个垂直 SaaS 或者垂直服务科技公司，然后把所有新的 AI 技术融入和构建到这个垂直领域里。它们有机会变得增速极快、盈利能力极强、人员效率更高——光成本结构就能降下来。

turns.en: I think that there's a great investment opportunity there. I think it's difficult for someone who's not in the market to assess because it's hard to see and it's hard to believe that maybe a name that people might say negative things about because they're an old business could reinvent themselves and become a great hot new business but with an old brand. That is happening in our market. We're starting to see some acquisitions over the last quarter. I think we saw three
turns.zh: 我觉得这是一个非常好的投资机会。但很难让不在行业里的人判断，因为很难看到、也很难相信——一个大家可能因为觉得它是老企业而说负面的名字，竟然能脱胎换骨变成一个很火的新业务，只是挂着老品牌。这确实在我们的市场里发生着。上季度开始有一些并购了，我记得有三笔

turns.en: of that type of business for very high exit multiples because they generated new technologies and were able to with their expertise and their knowledge of that sector and that workforce and everything to create an application that would automate a lot of that with AI. I would say majority of the businesses are going to be more buyout exits where you'll see lower growth but higher profitability over time. I think that the tech buyout funds, if they execute well,
turns.zh: 这类公司的交易，退出倍数非常高，因为它们创造了新技术，凭借自己的专业知识和对那个行业、那支团队的了解，做了一个能用 AI 自动化很多流程的应用。我觉得大部分公司未来更多是并购退出（buyout exit），增长率低一些但盈利能力会更高。技术类并购基金如果执行得好，

turns.en: will be able to go into sectors and aggregate up multiple companies in a sector and then operate them for cashflow rather than revenue growth. It's really interesting. Things are moving really quickly. Innovation is happening at a breakneck speed right now. It also strikes me that being a risk allocator in this environment has a lot of opportunities but also strikes me something that's really hard. That's right. I think one of the things that I've appreciated over time is just
turns.zh: 就能深入某个行业，把行业内多家公司聚合起来，然后以现金流而非收入增长为目标来运营。真的很有意思。变化非常快，创新正在以疯狂的速度推进。同时我也觉得，在这样的环境里做一个风险配置者，机会很多，但也真的很难。是的。我觉得随着时间推移我越来越体会到一件事，就是

turns.en: portfolio construction matters and looking at your positions and risk levels in the positions and then sizing them correctly to build a real institutional portfolio model around risk return.
turns.zh: 组合构建很重要，你要看每个头寸里的风险水平，然后正确配置仓位大小，建立一个围绕风险收益的真正机构级组合模型。

turns.en: Also, exit timing and then your multiple buy investment as well as an aggregated portfolio matters in this environment. We think more than it did before because of all the different cross currents and innovation going on in our market. If you can size things correctly with the risk return whole period multiple and IRR assumptions and you can get those somewhat right, then on an aggregated basis you diversify a lot of the loss rates because this market has more loss rates
turns.zh: 另外在这种环境下，退出时机、买入倍数、以及整个组合层面的表现比以前更重要了——因为我们的市场里各种力量在交叉碰撞、创新不断。如果你能正确地配置仓位，用风险收益、整个周期的倍数和 IRR 假设去做测算，并且大致能估对，那在组合层面你就能分散掉很多损失率，因为这个市场的损失率比

turns.en: than almost any other equity market in terms of just losing capital and transactions. Let's go back to the origin story. It's in the late 90s. This is even before you've helped create the market for venture secondaries. You're an entrepreneur. Tell us about what you're doing, what you're creating. I moved to Silicon Valley in the end of 95. I started my career in the valley as sleeping on the floor of the office, doing a startup software company with my brother. I didn't
turns.zh: 几乎所有其他股票市场都要高——纯粹从资本损失和交易失败的角度看。我们来聊聊你的创业故事吧。那是90年代末，甚至在你帮助创造风投二手这个市场之前。你是个创业者——跟我们说说你当时在做什么、在创建什么。我95年底搬到了硅谷，一开始在硅谷创业就是睡办公室地板，跟我兄弟一起做一个软件初创公司。我没有

turns.en: have much technical experience. I had to learn on the job with my brother sitting next to me selling software to engineers, which was a great experience because it taught me so many different things about software development and about engineering and about technology. You didn't end up being a software engineer. You ended up being effectively an asset management entrepreneur. I'm sure those experiences are really helpful for you as you founded
turns.zh: 什么技术经验。我必须在工作中学习——我兄弟就坐我旁边，我负责卖软件给工程师。这是一段很好的经历，因为它教会了我很多关于软件开发、工程和技术的东西。你最终没有成为软件工程师，而是成了一个资产管理领域的创业者。我相信这些经历在你创建

turns.en: an investing business and started backing the types of entrepreneurs like you and your brother were before that. Yeah, I was fortunate that I had two different startups with my brother, so I was able to learn all the things we did wrong first and try to fix them in the second one.
turns.zh: 一家投资公司、开始支持像你和兄弟当年那样的创业者时，非常有帮助。是的，我很幸运跟我兄弟做了两个不同的创业项目，所以第一个踩过的所有坑，都能在第二个里试着修正。

turns.en: But those experiences translated really well into technology investing, understanding companies at the company level and connecting with the entrepreneurs and the management teams at their level because that's where I came from. And that's helped me because I could understand the risks and understand the people side of the business a little bit better than most.
turns.zh: 但那些经历很好地转化到了科技投资里——从公司层面理解一家企业，跟创业者和管理团队在他们那个层次上对话，因为我就是从那里来的。这帮了我，因为我能比大多数人更好地理解风险，也更理解一个生意里'人'的那一面。

turns.en: Yeah, so after your second exit, you decided to take a different path. You embarked on what became venture secondaries. As an investment strategy, you talked to us about how that came about. I mean, the market didn't really exist at that moment in time. Yeah, I think the first two companies I had with my brother too, it was very similar where we started the companies before there was a real market. That's a blessing and a curse. And so when we started investing, originally, I was doing
turns.zh: 好，在你第二次退出之后，你决定走一条不同的路——开启了后来变成风投二手份额的征程。作为投资策略，跟我们聊聊它是怎么来的吧，当时这个市场其实并不存在。是的，我觉得跟我兄弟做的前两家公司也很类似——我们是在市场还没形成之前就开始做了。这既是好事也是挑战。一开始做投资的时候，我其实是在做

turns.en: angel investing. And when the NASDAQ collapse and the whole dot com bubble blew up, that whole capital market event caused us to relook at the venture business and see how we could make money in a very dislocated distress environment. And that's when we started calling and talking to other investors in the asset class and seeing if we could provide liquidity and buy them out of their positions. So Hans, this is the back in the time when we got to know each other when I was
turns.zh: 天使投资。然后 NASDAQ 崩盘、互联网泡沫破裂，整个资本市场事件让我们重新审视风投这个行业，看怎么在严重错配和困境环境里赚钱。于是我们开始给这个资产类别里的其他投资人打电话、找他们聊，看能不能给他们提供流动性、把他们的手头仓位买过来。所以 Hans，当年我们认识的时候，我正在

turns.en: looking after our secondaries platform and you were focused on venture. And I was really intrigued by this idea. But at the time, we really didn't have the expertise or the network that you had.
turns.zh: 管理我们的二手份额平台，而你专注于风投领域。当时这个概念非常吸引我，但我们确实没有你那样的专业知识和网络。

turns.en: And it was very clear to me right away that you had a different approach to this market. How big did you think this could become back then? I think we all had doubts of whether it was going to be like an episodic opportunity to create liquidity for kind of the dot com collapse, or it would be a structural feature of the market that over time would grow. I personally thought that it was going to become something more structural over time just because the secondary
turns.zh: 我很早就看出来了，你对这个市场有不同的切入方式。那时候你觉得这个市场能有多大？我觉得大家都有过怀疑——它到底只是一次性的机会，给互联网泡沫破裂创造一点流动性，还是会成为市场的一个结构性特征，随着时间推移不断成长。我个人倾向于认为它会变成一个更结构性的东西，因为二级

turns.en: market and every other market is sometimes bigger than the primary market. Most of the time it is. And so I always had a kind of inner feeling that this market could be a lot bigger than people thought. But I'd say the first kind of five to 10 years between 2000 and 2000 and maybe nine, there were a lot of doubts in the venture business about a 10-year period of people saying, hey, is that just a small market opportunity that's going to go away? Or is this something
turns.zh: 市场在任何其他资产类别里有时候都比一级市场大，多数时候确实是这样。所以我一直有一种内在感觉——这个市场可以比大家想象的更大。但2000年到2009年左右的前五到十年，风投行业里有很多怀疑，持续了大概十年：'这会不会就是一个很小的机会，很快就没了？还是说它真的会长成

turns.en: that structurally might develop over time into a big part of the market? So luckily, I stuck it out and saw the market grow and compound over a long period of time and become a really massive market.
turns.zh: 一个市场的大板块，随着时间结构性地发展起来？'幸运的是我坚持了下来，看着这个市场在很长的时间里增长、复利，变成了一个非常大的市场。

turns.en: Yeah, I'd say it worked out just fine. How big do you think the venture secondary market could become over time? Yeah, that's one of the things that's been really interesting being part of XIG is just looking at the buyout market and looking at the venture growth market. I think that our division has a different kind of more on the ground perspective here. The venture and growth part of the market is becoming large. It's becoming almost the same size as the buyout market.
turns.zh: 确实做得挺好的。你觉得风投二手市场长期能有多大？嗯，这确实是我们身处这个行业最有意思的一点——去看看并购基金（buyout）市场和风投成长期的市场。我觉得我们这块视角更接地气一些。风投和成长期市场的规模已经接近并购市场了。

turns.en: It's getting to the point where our NAV and our market is similar. And so we think that the venture growth market on the secondary side of the market can be larger than the primary side of the market. And we're still at a place in time today where our estimates of the venture secondary market are around $170 billion or so this year when the primary market might be, you know, this year might even do a trillion of invested capital. And so if you look at that
turns.zh: 已经到了我们的 NAV 跟整个市场规模差不多的地步了。所以我们认为风投成长期在二级端的规模可以超过一级。但今天我们的估算，今年风投二手大概1700亿美元左右，而一级市场——今年可能投出一万亿美元。如果从这个角度看

turns.en: historically, if you average things out, the primary market is somewhere between 300 and 500 billion over the last five to 10 years. And so we still have a nice kind of multiple on our market to grow. In all of the other asset classes, the secondary market is larger than the primary market.
turns.zh: 历史数据来看，过去5到10年平均，一级市场大概在3000到5000亿美元。所以我们的二级市场还有很大的倍数增长空间。在所有其他资产类别里，二级市场都比一级市场大。

turns.en: And so that's exciting. And one thing that's interesting in our market that's starting to happen is that even participants in the secondary market are starting to get liquidity through secondaries, which historically had never happened, right? Because the secondary market didn't really exist as an option. And then it became an option. You had a situation where there was the primary market transaction and then a secondary market transaction. But you didn't have a secondary
turns.zh: 所以这是令人兴奋的。我们市场里有一个有意思的事正在发生——即便是二级市场的参与者，也开始通过二手份额获得流动性，这在历史上从未有过。以前二级市场根本不是一个选项，后来变成了一个选项。过去你可能是一级市场一笔交易、然后二级市场一笔交易，但你不会看到

turns.en: market transaction that in turn also did a secondary market transaction. And we're starting to see that happening too. So that's the multiplier effect of why the market can be bigger than the primary market. And we're seeing that now all over the market. Hans, one of the things we're seeing right now is a lot more transparency in the private markets. And so in some of these secondaries where there are employee tenders or in primary rounds, people understand the valuations
turns.zh: 二级市场交易本身再去做一笔二手交易。这个我们现在也开始看到了，这就是为什么这个市场能比一级更大的乘数效应。我们在市场上到处都看到了。Hans，我们现在看到的一件事是私募市场的透明度大大提高了——在一些二手交易里，比如员工回购要约或者在一级融资轮里，大家知道了估值，

turns.en: and you see more and more trades happening in the secondary market at some of these valuations. Is that leading to more volume? What is the impact on the private markets?
turns.zh: 然后你看到越来越多的二手交易就是在这些估值附近成交。这是在推动更大的交易量吗？对私募市场有什么影响？

turns.en: Yeah, historically, there weren't that many transactions, right? So it was hard to determine what the right price would be if you were a seller or if you were a buyer. And I think today with more volume and more transparency, that's just making both buyers and sellers more comfortable to transact. And so I do think that that is driving more volume in the market.
turns.zh: 是的，以前交易量不够多，不管是买方还是卖方都很难确定合理价格。现在有了更大的交易量和更高的透明度，买卖双方都更安心去做交易了，所以我觉得这确实在驱动更多的交易量。

turns.en: So I want to pivot and talk about a personal decision you made in the last year. Obviously, things have changed from the days when you had a sleeping bag under your desk and you were building companies, maybe thinking a little bit more about your rent payment and how you're going to take your girlfriend out to a nice dinner. You decided to sell Street Ventures to Goldman Sachs a year ago. What changed over that period of time? What led to that transaction? Well, I think success
turns.zh: 我想换一个话题，聊聊你过去一年做的一个个人决定。显然，跟你把睡袋放在办公桌下面、创业初期还在操心房租和怎么带女朋友去吃顿好饭的日子，已经完全不同了。一年前你决定把 Industry Ventures 卖给 Goldman Sachs。这段时间里什么改变了？是什么促成了这笔交易？嗯，我觉得是'成功'

turns.en: changed. The definition of success changes through your life. The first phase of this business, like the others, were just get it successful, right? I've always looked at businesses as like their own kind of being in their own person. So it's out of the gate, you've got to get it self-sustaining, right? It's like having your kids go off and I graduate from college and get their own job and stop paying their allowance. So that was our first phase. And then I think the
turns.zh: 的定义变了。成功的定义在人生不同阶段是不一样的。做这门生意的第一个阶段，跟所有其他生意一样，就是让它活下来。我一直把企业当作有自己生命的个体来看——刚起步的时候，你得让它能自我造血。就像孩子大学毕业、自己找到工作、你不再给他零花钱一样。这是第一阶段。然后我觉得

turns.en: second phase was go execute and build out the business really well and get it to have a nice growth rate, nice profitability, nice returns to all the LPs, nice repeatability with the investors re-upping, nice repeatability with different counterparties with GPs, entrepreneurs and whatnot and then kind of grow and scale it in the repeatable ways, which is what we did.
turns.zh: 第二阶段就是把业务做好做扎实，获得好的增长率、好的盈利、给所有 LP 好的回报、让投资人愿意重复出资、跟不同的 GP、创业者、对手方都有好的可复制性，然后用可重复的方式去增长和扩张——这就是我们做的。

turns.en: And then it got to a point where we had the third phase of success, which is our markets growing, our markets institutionalizing. Should we be more institutional? Should we scale this more?
turns.zh: 然后到了第三阶段的成功：我们的市场在增长、在机构化。我们是不是应该变得更机构化？是不是应该进一步扩大规模？

turns.en: If we're going to scale this more is 0, 1 plus 1 is 3 out there in terms of another firm like ours that's bigger, that's already built everything that we've wanted to go build in our plans.
turns.zh: 如果要进一步做大规模，1+1能不能等于3——就是说外面有没有一家跟我们类似但更大的公司，已经把我们计划中想做的一切都建好了？

turns.en: And I think, you know, luckily we found this working relationship with Goldman to be so great that over time we just sort of folded in our division. I mean, we've been working together for 20 years. You know, you built a large part of this division from scratch and a secondary fund as well. And so there's a lot of history here. And I think that that mattered. And then Goldman itself had owned part of our management company and you saw us operate and hit our plans over a
turns.zh: 我觉得，幸运的是，我们发现跟 Goldman 的合作关系非常好，所以随着时间推移，我们自然就把业务并进去了。我们合作了20年。你知道，你亲手从零建设了这个业务板块，还建了一支二手基金，这里面有很多历史渊源，我觉得这很重要。而且 Goldman 本身就持有我们管理公司的一部分股份，他们看着我们运营和按计划完成了

turns.en: period of seven years because we had quarterly meetings over that period. And so there just became trust during that period as well. And so we saw this as like a third phase of making sure that we're successful for our investors. We're successful for our team members. The business itself can be continuing to compete at an extremely high rate in terms of its competitiveness and kind of take this business to a next level, which I think we're doing now internally here
turns.zh: 一个周期七年，因为那段时间我们每个季度都有会议，所以在这个过程中建立了信任。我们把这看作第三阶段的成功——确保我们对投资人成功、对团队成员成功，让企业本身能够以极高的竞争力持续竞争，把这门生意带到一个新层次——我觉得我们现在作为 Goldman 内部的一部分正在做到

turns.en: as part of Goldman. Yeah, I totally agree. And for me, it's been so much fun to bring this together. First of all, getting to know what is an absolutely terrific team of people in industry ventures. We've just been so impressed. Obviously, you and I have known each other for 25 years, but it's great to get to know the broader cross-section of people at industry ventures. And if you look at the venture secondary market, as you're saying,
turns.zh: 这一点。是的，我完全同意。对我来说，把这件事促成真的非常开心。首先，我认识了 Industry Ventures 一支特别优秀的团队——我们印象非常深刻。当然你我认识25年了，但很高兴能认识 Industry Ventures 更多更广的人。如果你看风投二级市场，就像你说的，

turns.en: there's a lot more opportunity than there is capital right now. And I think that's a good backdrop for something where we can take the Goldman sourcing engine and add it to yours, which is hard to replicate with all the people that you have inside Silicon Valley with the network that you have. And so I think it's really exciting what can happen here. Let's just roll into the future here. It's 2030. What do you think this all looks like? I think it's going to look
turns.zh: 机会比资本多得多。我觉得这是一个很好的背景——我们可以把 Goldman 的项目搜索引擎加上你们的能力，你们在硅谷有那么多人、那么广的网络，这种能力是别人很难复制的。所以我觉得接下来能发生的事情真的让人兴奋。让我们跳到未来——假设是2030年，你觉得一切会是什么样子？我觉得会变得

turns.en: different every five years. Our market's evolved and changed, and so has all the other capital markets. Our market is kind of the driving force of AI in the world today. There are so many different opportunities, but one area that's kind of really fascinating that's going to, we think, create a lot of opportunity is the digital AI market and the physical AI market is going to collide. And so we're going to see a lot of things in our real life, right, be AI-enabled
turns.zh: 每五年都不一样。我们的市场一直在演变，所有其他资本市场也是。我们的市场可以说是今天全球 AI 的驱动力。机会太多了，但有一个领域我们觉得特别吸引人、会创造大量机会——数字 AI 市场和实体 AI 市场正在碰撞融合。我们会看到很多现实生活中的事情变成 AI 驱动的，

turns.en: and live and work together with artificial intelligence in hardware formats in our daily lives. And so there's a huge opportunity there for entrepreneurs, and we're seeing a lot of innovation at the early stages there. I think you've also got healthcare is going to get transformed.
turns.zh: 以硬件形式融入我们的日常生活，跟 AI 共存共事。这里面对于创业者来说机会巨大，我们在早期就看到了很多创新。还有医疗健康——会被彻底变革。

turns.en: It already is starting to be transformed. And then financial services and the whole reindustrialization of the United States, you're seeing the military complex being transformed right now in terms of what is being used in the battlefield. And then you've got space, right? So there's a bunch of opportunities now with going to the moon or interplanetary travel or everything from mining to moon base. And so the satellite systems around the planet are obviously going to
turns.zh: 已经开始被变革了。然后是金融服务和美国的整个再工业化，军事领域正在被改变——战场上用的东西在变。还有太空——登月、星际旅行、从太空采矿到月球基地，各种机会。围绕地球的卫星体系肯定会

turns.en: change in the next five years in a dramatic way. Yeah, no shortage of excitement and change and innovation. And I can tell you I'm just so excited about working on this opportunity together in the next five, 10, 15 years, because one of the things we know for sure is there's going to be a lot of change, there's going to be a lot of innovation. And so therefore there's going to be a lot to do. Now, Hans, we like to finish these sessions with a lightning wrap.
turns.zh: 在未来五年发生戏剧性的变化。是的，永远不缺兴奋、变化和创新。我可以告诉你，我非常兴奋未来5年、10年、15年能一起抓住这个机遇，因为我们确定的一件事就是：一定会有很大的变化、很大的创新，因此一定会有很多事情可以做。好，Hans，我们每次节目最后都有一个快问快答（lightning round）环节。

turns.en: So I'm going to jump into that now. What is your greatest strength as an investor? turns.zh: 我们直接开始吧。你作为投资人最大的优势是什么？我觉得就是我在市场里所有环节都待过——我就像一个球员兼教练，场上每个位置我都做过：当过创始人、当过运营者、当过 LP、当过直接投资人、当过二手份额投资人、当过并购联合投资人，能看到硬币的所有面，从

turns.en: lifecycle of a company to fund how liquidity works and where it might come from, and then looking at the company from a company perspective, understanding how it's being operated. There's not many people I've met that have all those sets of experiences combined into one person.
turns.zh: 一个公司的生命周期来理解流动性是怎么运作的、可能从哪里来，然后站在公司角度看企业怎么运营的。我见过的人里，没有多少能集齐这些经历于一身的。

turns.en: And so I think that that's been my superpower. I can remember even 15 or 20 years ago talking about your reputation here within Goldman as one of the most sober and realistic prices of risk in the venture market. So I would definitely agree with that.

turns.en: Was it easier to build software companies or a fund management business? Definitely software companies. I think in the investment business, as you know, especially with the time period to
turns.zh: 做软件公司和做基金管理哪个更容易？绝对是软件公司。软件公司能很快得到产品市场契合度（product-market fit）的反馈、很快得到客户反馈。如果客户喜欢，能部署到业务里或者个人使用，成功或失败都很快速，处理起来更容易。我觉得投资行业——你也知道——尤其是退出周期

turns.en: exit in our market, proving out your track record, proving out you can make money, proving out you can make money at a certain IRR rate, which is more important now than ever compared to other asset classes and just proving you can invest correctly for the right risk return for the investor base. I think it's really hard. It's just the duration on it's difficult. And then in terms of doing that repeatedly over cycles, it's very difficult
turns.zh: 在我们市场里这么长，要证明自己——证明你能赚钱、能以某个 IRR 赚钱，这比其他资产类别现在更重要。你得证明你能为投资人正确把握风险收益。真的很难。光是周期长就很难。要跨周期反复做到，非常难——

turns.en: because you have drawdowns. We've had multiple drawdowns over the last 20 years and and compounding capital through drawdowns is difficult. What's the best piece of advice you've ever gotten? I had a good, good piece of advice a long time ago from a friend. He said, you know, because I asked him, you know, in your career, what was one of the most important things that you learned? And he said, if you're really good at something, keep doing it for extremely long
turns.zh: 因为会有回撤。过去20年我们经历了多次回撤，带着回撤做资本复利很难。你收到过最好的建议是什么？很久以前一个朋友给过我一条很好的建议。因为我问他：'你职业生涯里学到的最重要的东西是什么？'他说：如果你真的擅长某件事，就一直做，做非常非常长的

turns.en: period of time. You want to be working on the same in the same sector on the same set of problems over a long, long period of time. And if you're really good at it and you have a talent for it, what you'll find 20, 30 years later is that you'll become an expert in that area and everyone you've worked with during that period of time plus the people they know will come to you for a solution or advice or, you know, in our case, you know, investing opportunities. And that's proved
turns.zh: 时间。你要在同一个行业、同一类问题上花很长时间去做。如果你真的擅长、有天赋，20年、30年后你会发现自己成了那个领域的专家，所有跟你合作过的人、以及他们认识的人，都会来找你寻求解决方案、建议——在我们这行就是投资机会。这已经被证实

And so I couldn't think of a more exciting time that I've ever seen in the technology markets in my life. I agree. Hans, thanks for being with
turns.zh: 是对的。最后一个问题——你现在对世界上的什么事情感到兴奋？我觉得这是我见过的投资领域最激动人心的时刻。全球所有类别都在创新，这是一场全球性的创新事件，是一次平台级的变革。我觉得在各个领域我们才刚刚开始。我这辈子没见过比这更令人兴奋的科技市场了。我同意。Hans，感谢你今天
